docs.title: Design Analysis: Mapping Report (Workflow Manager)
docs.text:
Describes what the Mapping Report feature does and why, based on its design source. It does not define technical implementation.

Field Value Analysis ID DA-003 Feature Mapping Report (pdf-workflow / workflow-manager) Source Material branch: design, path: pdf-workflow/workflow-manager/design/v4/, commit: f5de2a0fbdac4033b2a8aecf523d15948c6801f5 Source Version 4 Analysis Version 1.1 Created By Business Agent workflow Created At 2026-09-08 Status Approved -- 16/16 requirements, BR-003 revised per direct feedback after PR #17 merged (see Review history) Related Epic Pending -- created at the Business PR stage Related Stories Pending -- created at the Business PR stage Business Owner Approval Approved 2026-09-08 -- see Review history

Supersedes DA-002 in intent, not in the formal sense -- DA-002 was deleted rather than marked Superseded, since it was built against the wrong source version entirely; this is a fresh run, not DA-002's successor version. It corrects two things DA-002 got wrong as a result -- see OBS-009.

docs.title: What this is
docs.text:
Workflows created by uploading a PDF get their page/section/field structure auto-extracted, with a confidence score attached to every proposed mapping. The Mapping Report is where a reviewer -- the only role this feature currently supports -- checks that extraction, corrects what's wrong, and fills in whatever it missed. This report only applies to the PDF-creation path; an LLM-based creation path is named in the source as a possible future reuse target, not built now.

Source reviewed: SRC-003, pdf-workflow/workflow-manager/design/v4/README.md (the "Mapping Report" section, plus the shared Scope note, Known UX issues, Interactions & behavior, and State management sections where they describe this screen specifically).

Source limitations, stated up front: mobile/tablet layout for the mapping table was explicitly deferred by the source itself, resolved by direct clarification to horizontal scroll rather than stacked cards; no numeric bound is stated for page, section, field, or FieldGroup sub-field counts; the exact navigation trigger into the report and the zero-mappings empty state were both unstated in the source, both resolved by direct clarification below.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Automatic extraction assigns every proposed mapping a confidence score rather than treating extraction as reliable, and the source names extraction as carrying risk when discussing the related LLM-based creation path ("same class of risk as PDF extraction -- the LLM can misread intent"). Without a review step, an incorrectly extracted or mapped field would carry through unchecked into a workflow used to collect real submissions.

Evidence: OBS-026. Strongly Implied, Medium confidence.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
Catch and correct an incorrect or low-confidence field extraction before a workflow goes live to collect real submissions.

Evidence: OBS-026. Strongly Implied, Medium confidence.

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text: Not defined in source. Decision Required -- see DEC-005, owner: Business Owner.

docs.title: Reviewing the mapping
docs.text:
Before touching anything, the reviewer sees five stat tiles -- Total, High (≥80% confidence), Medium (50-79%), Low (<50%), and Average -- each colored by its band, so they know at a glance how much attention this workflow's mapping needs.

Below that, the mapping is a collapsible three-level hierarchy: Page, then Section (a page can hold more than one), then Field as the leaf row. A field row shows the original PDF text, its extracted kind (what the element actually is), the Target Type it's mapped to, a confidence percentage, and a source icon (llm/manual), alongside edit and unlink controls -- the same information whether shown as a table row or, in the deferred Card view, a card.

Search is live text matching with no submit button; a confidence segmented control (All/High/Medium/Low) narrows the same view. Both apply at the field level -- a Section only stays visible if it still has a matching field or its own heading matches, and a Page only stays visible if it still has a visible Section. Filtering never leaves an empty Section or Page on screen.

Table view only, for this phase. The design fully specifies a Card view -- same data, card layout, sharing all state (search, filter, an in-progress edit) with Table view -- but building it is deferred; see BR-003 for why, and BRULE-005 for the modeling constraint that keeps it addable later without rework. Below roughly 900px, the table uses horizontal scroll rather than a stacked-card row layout -- the source explicitly left this open rather than silently picking one; see BRULE-008.

docs.title: Editing a mapped field
docs.text:
Every mapping has a kind -- what the PDF element actually is (heading, description, field, field-group, or custom) -- and maps to a targetType (Section, Content, Field, FieldGroup, or Custom), shown to the reviewer as a compound label like Field-Date or Field-List-3x (item count) so sub-cases are distinguishable without opening the row (exact label format: BR-005). A mapping can only ever be remapped within its own kind -- a field can't become a FieldGroup; whether the UI actively blocks the attempt or simply never lists the incompatible option is a technical detail, not a business one.

Clicking the pencil expands that row in place with controls specific to its kind -- a single Text box for headings/descriptions, Label + type for a Field, Label + an editable per-item list + Min/Max items for a FieldGroup, Label only for Custom. There is no dropdown-based remapping anywhere in the current design (BR-006). Only one row can be open for edit at a time, and every panel ends in an explicit Cancel or Save. Saving persists the change and shows a success toast; Cancel discards. Trying to navigate away -- switching rows, or leaving the page -- while an edit is dirty prompts a discard-confirmation dialog first.

docs.title: JRN-001
docs.text: Review and correct a low-confidence field mapping. A reviewer filters to Low confidence, opens the first flagged field, corrects its label and type, and saves -- the panel closes, a toast confirms, and the row returns to its normal state. Uses CAP-002 and CAP-004. Registry: JOURNEY-REGISTRY.md / full record.

docs.title: Unlinking a mapping
docs.text: Clicking unlink opens a confirmation dialog before the mapping is removed -- and for a FieldGroup, the dialog names the specific sub-fields that would be lost, so the reviewer understands the actual cost before confirming.

docs.title: JRN-002
docs.text: Remove an incorrectly extracted field. A reviewer decides a 2-field FieldGroup mapping is entirely wrong, clicks unlink, sees a dialog naming both sub-fields that would be lost, and confirms -- the mapping is removed. Uses CAP-005. Registry: JOURNEY-REGISTRY.md / full record.

docs.title: Manually adding structure, and starting a new workflow
docs.text:
"+ Add page" appends a new, empty, auto-numbered page with no confirmation dialog; "+ Add section" (title required, description optional) and "+ Add field" (label required, type selected) follow the same low-ceremony inline-form pattern, each with Add disabled until its required field is filled. A manually-added item groups exactly like something the extraction found for real -- a manually-added section gets a synthetic mapped heading at 100% confidence, so it's indistinguishable in structure from an extracted one.

This same starting surface is also where a brand-new workflow lands, right after its Workflow Settings are saved -- not a PDF-specific behavior. This refines the source's own "Scope note," which reads as PDF-only for the whole screen: only the confidence-review chrome genuinely is PDF-only (see BR-015 below); the structure editor underneath is reused across creation paths. See BR-016 and GAP-003.

docs.title: JRN-003
docs.text: Add a section the extraction missed. A reviewer expands a page with no sections yet, clicks "+ Add section," enters a title, and clicks Add -- the new section appears immediately, grouped under that page exactly like an extracted one. Uses CAP-006. Registry: JOURNEY-REGISTRY.md / full record.

docs.title: Removing empty structure, and reordering
docs.text: A page or section only shows a delete option once it has zero children -- nothing to lose, so no confirmation dialog either; there's no error state to design here, since the action simply isn't offered otherwise. Every page, section, and field also gets up/down controls to move it one position among its siblings, stored as an explicit per-level override list rather than a full re-index every time (the exact storage mechanism is a technical question, not a business one -- see TECH-002).

docs.title: Who sees this
docs.text:
The confidence-review chrome -- stat tiles, confidence filter, source (llm/manual) tags -- only shows for workflows created via the PDF path; it's meaningless without an extraction step to review (BR-015). Manually-created workflows don't get that chrome, though they do land on the same structure editor described above (BR-016). An LLM-created path is named in the source as a possible future reuse target, not built now.

No permission or role distinction is represented anywhere in the Mapping Report material itself -- one reviewer role covers everything described here. The wider product does show org-level "Members"/"Billing" controls, implying a multi-user org, but whether reviewing or editing mappings is restricted to certain org members is left open until a login/auth capability exists -- not a remaining open question, but also not yet actionable as a requirement.

Each mapping arrives already carrying a kind and a confidence score, extracted from the PDF before the reviewer ever sees the report -- what mechanism produces that extraction is a technical question for the Technical Agent stage, not a business concern here (see TECH-001).

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Every Business Requirement's full statement, acceptance criteria, and evidence classification -- in the same order the narrative above introduces them, not flat ID order. Click a BR-XXX reference from the narrative to jump straight here.

docs.title: BR-001
docs.text:
Show extraction confidence summary.

The product must show the reviewer, before any interaction, how many mappings fall into each confidence band (High/Medium/Low), the total count, and the average confidence.

Given a workflow's Mapping Report is opened
When the page renders
Then five stat tiles are shown: Total, High, Medium, Low, and Average confidence
And each tile's top border is colored by its confidence band

Evidence: OBS-001. Explicit, High confidence.

docs.title: BR-002
docs.text:
Browse mappings via Page → Section → Field hierarchy.

The product must let the reviewer browse mappings as a collapsible three-level hierarchy (Page, then Section, then Field), where a page may contain more than one section.

Given a workflow with multiple pages, and at least one page with multiple sections
When the reviewer views the mapping
Then pages, sections, and fields are shown as a collapsible three-level hierarchy
And a page correctly shows more than one section when the source data has more than one

Evidence: OBS-006, OBS-007. Explicit, High confidence.

docs.title: BR-003
docs.text:
Table view, with state that would survive a future view toggle.

The product must provide the mapping review as a Table view, with search, confidence filter, and in-progress-edit state modeled independently of presentation -- so a Card view, if and when it's built, can be added without restructuring this state.

Given the reviewer has an active search term, a confidence filter, or a field row expanded for edit
Then that state is held independently of how it's rendered (not coupled to Table-view-specific markup)
And Table view is the only rendering built and shown in this phase -- no Card view toggle is presented
Note: the source's own criterion (switching Table↔Card without losing state) becomes the acceptance test for whenever Card view is picked up later -- not dropped, just not exercised by this phase's build.

Evidence: OBS-003, OBS-025. Explicit (Table/Card sync design), narrowed by Human Provided input (Table-only for now) -- see GAP-004.

Narrowed 2026-09-08, not removed -- see GAP-004 for the full PR #17 review history.

docs.title: BR-004
docs.text:
Search and filter by confidence, with hierarchical visibility.

The product must let the reviewer search mappings by text and filter by confidence band, applying at the field level, with a Section shown only if it still contains a visible Field and a Page shown only if it still contains a visible Section.

Given a workflow with fields at multiple confidence levels across multiple sections and pages
When the reviewer selects the "Low" confidence filter
Then only fields below 50% confidence remain visible
And any Section with no remaining visible field is hidden
And any Page with no remaining visible Section is hidden

Evidence: OBS-002, OBS-013. Explicit, High confidence.

docs.title: BR-005
docs.text:
Show a compound Target Type label; no cross-kind remapping.

The product must show each mapping's target type as a compound label combining the display type and a kind-specific detail (e.g. field type, item count, or app-component name), and must not offer a remap that would cross into an incompatible kind.

Given a field-group mapping with 3 sub-fields
When the reviewer views its Target Type tag
Then the tag reads "Field-List-3x" (or the equivalent compound label for its actual item count)

Given a field-kind row
When the reviewer looks for a remap option
Then only Field-type targets are offered, never a Section, Content, FieldGroup, or Custom target

Evidence: OBS-004, OBS-005. Explicit, High confidence.

docs.title: BR-006
docs.text:
Edit a mapped field with kind-specific controls.

The product must let the reviewer edit a mapped field's details in place, using controls appropriate to its kind.

Given a field-group mapping is opened for edit
Then the edit panel shows a Label input, a per-item field list (each with its own label, type, and remove control, plus "+ Add field"), and Min items/Max items inputs

Given a heading or description mapping is opened for edit
Then the edit panel shows a single Text textarea and nothing else

Given any mapping's pencil icon is clicked
Then the row expands in place -- no dropdown/select-based remapping is ever offered

Evidence: OBS-008, OBS-009, OBS-010. Explicit, High confidence -- directly re-verified against the real v4 text; no dropdown anywhere in the current source.

docs.title: BR-007
docs.text:
One edit panel open at a time, with explicit Save/Cancel.

The product must allow only one field's edit panel open at a time (opening a new one collapses the previous), and every edit panel must end in an explicit Cancel or Save action.

Given field row A is expanded for edit
When the reviewer clicks the pencil icon on field row B
Then row A collapses without saving
And row B expands with its own edit controls

Given a field's edit panel is open
When the reviewer clicks Save
Then the change persists and a success toast confirms it

Given a field's edit panel is open
When the reviewer clicks Cancel
Then the edit is discarded and the row returns to its prior state

Evidence: OBS-010. Explicit, High confidence.

docs.title: BR-014
docs.text:
Warn before discarding an unsaved edit.

The product must prompt the reviewer with a discard-confirmation before losing an in-progress, unsaved field edit, whether by switching rows or navigating away.

Given a field's edit panel is open with unsaved changes
When the reviewer attempts to navigate away (switch rows, or leave the page)
Then a discard-confirmation dialog appears
And the navigation completes only if the reviewer confirms discarding

Evidence: OBS-011. Explicit, High confidence.

docs.title: BR-008
docs.text:
Unlink a mapping with cost-aware confirmation.

The product must, when the reviewer unlinks a mapping, confirm before removing it, and for a FieldGroup mapping the confirmation must name the sub-fields that would be lost.

Given a FieldGroup mapping with 2 sub-fields
When the reviewer clicks unlink
Then a confirmation dialog opens naming the 2 sub-fields that would be lost
And the mapping is removed only if the reviewer confirms

Evidence: OBS-009, OBS-011. Explicit, High confidence.

docs.title: BR-009
docs.text:
Manually add a page.

The product must let the reviewer add a new, empty, auto-numbered page with no confirmation dialog, rendered expanded and ready to receive a section.

Given the reviewer clicks "+ Add page"
Then a new page is appended, numbered one higher than the current maximum page number
And it renders expanded, showing only a "+ Add section" prompt
And no confirmation dialog is shown

Evidence: OBS-014, OBS-012. Explicit, High confidence.

docs.title: BR-010
docs.text:
Manually add a section.

The product must let the reviewer add a new section to a page via an inline form (title required, description optional), which creates a section that groups with extracted sections identically (a synthetic mapped heading at full confidence).

Given a page with zero or more existing sections
When the reviewer adds a section with a title and no description
Then the Add action is available only once the title is non-empty
And the new section appears grouped under that page exactly like an extracted section, at 100% confidence

Evidence: OBS-015. Explicit, High confidence.

docs.title: BR-011
docs.text:
Manually add a field.

The product must let the reviewer add a new field to a section via an inline form (label required, type selected), appearing immediately in the correct position with no reload.

Given a section is expanded
When the reviewer adds a field with a label and a type
Then the Add action is available only once the label is non-empty
And the new field appears immediately after that section's existing fields, with no page reload

Evidence: OBS-016. Explicit, High confidence.

docs.title: BR-016
docs.text:
Provide the structure editor as the starting surface for a new workflow.

The product must, after a new workflow's settings are saved, land the user on the same page/section/field structure editor used for PDF-mapping review (empty), letting them begin building structure via "+ Add page" -- regardless of the workflow's eventual creation path.

Given a new workflow's settings have just been saved
When the user is returned to the workflow
Then they land on the page/section/field structure editor, empty, showing only a "+ Add section" prompt
And they can begin building structure immediately via "+ Add page" / "+ Add section"

Evidence: OBS-021, OBS-022. Human Provided, from direct clarification on PR #17. This also resolved what were previously open Decisions about the report's entry trigger and its zero-mappings empty state -- see GAP-003.

docs.title: BR-012
docs.text:
Delete only empty structure.

The product must offer a delete action on a page or section only when it has zero children, and must require no confirmation when it does.

Given a page with zero sections
Then a delete (trash) icon is shown next to its expand toggle

Given a page with at least one section
Then no delete icon is shown for that page

Evidence: OBS-017. Explicit, High confidence.

docs.title: BR-013
docs.text:
Reorder pages, sections, and fields.

The product must let the reviewer move a page, section, or field one position among its siblings, without requiring every item at that level to be re-specified.

Given three fields in one section, in order A, B, C
When the reviewer clicks the down-reorder control on field A
Then the order becomes B, A, C
And fields not explicitly moved retain their natural relative order

Evidence: OBS-018. Explicit, High confidence.

docs.title: BR-015
docs.text:
Restrict confidence-review chrome to PDF-created workflows.

The product must show the confidence-review elements of this screen only for workflows created via the PDF path; these are meaningless without an extraction step to review. An LLM-created path, if built later, is a separate future scope decision, not covered by this unconditionally.

Given a workflow created via the "Upload PDF" path
Then its Mapping Report is available and meaningful (confidence, source, kind all populated)

Given a workflow created via "Manually create"
Then the confidence-review chrome (stat tiles, confidence filter, source tags) is not shown --
but the underlying structure editor is still used as its starting surface (see BR-016)

Evidence: OBS-019. Explicit, High confidence.

Narrowed 2026-09-08, not removed -- see GAP-003 for the full PR #17 review history.

docs.title: Open Decisions
docs.text:
The first four were resolved 2026-09-08, directly on PR #17's review -- per Manali's stated preference that resolution happen inside the PR review itself, not in chat or as separate Issues.

  • DEC-001: navigation trigger into the Mapping Report -- Resolved, three real entry paths (PDF conversion, reopening an existing mapping, starting a new workflow from scratch).
  • DEC-002: empty state for zero mappings -- Resolved, via the new-workflow flow (BR-016).
  • DEC-003: mobile/tablet table layout -- Resolved, horizontal scroll, not stacked cards (BRULE-008).
  • DEC-004: org role/permission requirements -- Resolved (deferred), no permission layer until login/auth exists.
  • DEC-005: success metric for this feature -- Open, owner: Business Owner.

Only two Technical Unknowns remain (TECH-001, TECH-002) -- not business decisions, not a blocker to Business Requirements; for the Technical Agent stage. DEC-005 (success metric, added 2026-09-25) is open too, but doesn't block Business Requirements either -- it affects how success is measured after launch, not what gets built.

docs.title: Not built yet
docs.text:
• Card view -- fully designed, deferred for this phase. See BR-003, GAP-004.
  • LLM-created workflow path -- named in the source as a future reuse target, not this pass.
  • Org-level permissions -- deferred until login/auth exists. See DEC-004.
  • Error/failure states for save, add, delete, and reorder -- not represented in the source, not assumed.
  • Extraction mechanism and reorder-list storage -- technical questions, for the Technical Agent. See TECH-001, TECH-002.
  • This analysis covers only the Mapping Report feature-slice of the v4 drop. The same drop's other screens (Dashboard, Settings Dialog, Page Editor, full auth flow) are out of scope here and, per DESIGN-HANDOFF-BUNDLE-FORMAT-SPEC.md section 6.2, registered and analyzed separately if/when taken up.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text: Grouped by the Journey that actually needs them -- a capability's real purpose only makes sense next to the goal it serves, per ARTIFACT-RELATIONSHIP-MODEL.md section 3.1. Listed here as a stable entry point for the Business Requirements stage, which will need to reference these directly when grouping Stories. Full evidence for each lives in its own record, linked below -- not repeated here.

docs.title: Serving JRN-001 -- Review and correct a low-confidence field mapping
docs.text: A reviewer narrows down to what needs fixing, then corrects it in place -- these two capabilities are the whole journey, back to back.

docs.title: CAP-002
docs.text: Filter and Search Mappings. Let the reviewer narrow a potentially large mapping down to what needs checking. (↩ used by BR-004) Registry: CAPABILITY-REGISTRY.md / full record.

docs.title: CAP-004
docs.text: Edit a Mapped Field's Details. Let the reviewer correct what the extraction got wrong, with controls appropriate to what kind of element it is. (↩ used by BR-005, BR-006, BR-007, BR-014) Registry: CAPABILITY-REGISTRY.md / full record.

docs.title: Serving JRN-002 -- Remove an incorrectly extracted field
CAP-005
docs.text: Unlink an Incorrect Mapping. Let the reviewer remove a wrong mapping while understanding its cost. (↩ used by BR-008) Registry: CAPABILITY-REGISTRY.md / full record.

docs.title: Serving JRN-003 -- Add a section the extraction missed
CAP-006
docs.text: Manually Add Structure. Let the reviewer fill in whatever the extraction missed, and let a new workflow begin from the same structure editor regardless of creation path. (↩ used by BR-009, BR-010, BR-011, BR-016) Registry: CAPABILITY-REGISTRY.md / full record.

docs.title: Not yet tied to a Journey
docs.text: Identified as real capabilities from the source, but none of DA-003's three recorded journeys happens to walk through them end to end -- an honest gap this document surfaces rather than hides, not something to force-fit into a journey that doesn't actually need it. Worth a journey each if this feature-slice is revisited.

docs.title: CAP-001
docs.text: Review Extraction Confidence and Structure. Let the reviewer gauge how much attention a workflow's mapping needs before working through it in detail. (↩ used by BR-001, BR-002) Registry: CAPABILITY-REGISTRY.md / full record.

docs.title: CAP-003
docs.text: Switch Between Table and Card Views. Let the reviewer choose a layout without losing filter or edit state -- Table view only is built this phase. (↩ used by BR-003) Registry: CAPABILITY-REGISTRY.md / full record. Card view isn't built this phase, so no journey exercises a view toggle.

docs.title: CAP-007
docs.text: Remove Empty Structure. Let the reviewer clean up structure that's no longer needed, without risking accidental data loss. (↩ used by BR-012) Registry: CAPABILITY-REGISTRY.md / full record.

docs.title: CAP-008
docs.text: Reorder Structure. Let the reviewer fix the order pages, sections, or fields appear in. (↩ used by BR-013) Registry: CAPABILITY-REGISTRY.md / full record.

docs.title: Evidence and Traceability
docs.text: Reference material. Each entry below is what an "Evidence" link above jumps to -- not needed to understand the feature, needed to audit a specific claim. Every entry ends with a "used by" link back to whatever cited it.

docs.title: OBS-001
docs.text: Five stat tiles show Total / High (≥80%) / Medium (50-79%) / Low (<50%) / Avg confidence, each with a top border colored by its band. Explicit, High. (↩ used by BR-001)

docs.title: OBS-002
docs.text: Filters are two rows: search + "Created from" (PDF/LLM/Manual, demo-only) on row one, confidence + view toggle on row two; all four share one filter/view state. Explicit, High. (↩ used by BR-004)

docs.title: OBS-003
docs.text: The View toggle (Table/Cards) renders the exact same filtered/grouped data; switching never resets search, confidence filter, source filter, or an in-progress edit. Explicit, High. (↩ used by BR-003, BRULE-005)

docs.title: OBS-004
docs.text: Each mapping has a kind and maps to a target whose targetType is the discriminant; a kind can only remap within its own family. Explicit, High. (↩ used by BR-005, BRULE-001)

docs.title: OBS-005
docs.text: The Target Type shown to the reviewer is a compound label, e.g. Field-Text, Field-Date, Field-List-3x, Custom-App-signature-pad; description-kind rows show just Text. Explicit, High. (↩ used by BR-005)

docs.title: OBS-006
docs.text: The mapping view is a 3-level accordion: Page → Section → Field row (leaf); a page can have multiple sections. Explicit, High. (↩ used by BR-002)

docs.title: OBS-007
docs.text: A field row shows: PDF text, source kind tag, Target Type tag, Maps-to label, confidence %, source icon, edit and unlink icon buttons -- identical information in Table and Card view, laid out differently. Explicit, High. (↩ used by BR-002)

docs.title: OBS-008
docs.text: Source (Screens section): "No inline <select> remapping. The old 'pick a different target from a dropdown' pattern was removed. Instead, clicking the pencil expands the row in place" with kind-specific controls. Explicit, High. (↩ used by BR-006)

docs.title: OBS-009
docs.text: Source (Interactions & behavior section): "clicking the pencil expands the row/card in place with kind-specific fields... and Cancel/Save actions — there is no remap-via-dropdown; clicking unlink opens a confirm dialog (names the sub-field cost for FieldGroups) before removing the mapping." Explicit, High. Directly confirms OBS-008 and OBS-011. Verified 2026-09-08 against the actual v4 text: this replaces the retracted DA-002's finding, which quoted v2's contradicting dropdown-remap wording -- that wording no longer exists in v4. (↩ used by BR-006, BR-008)

docs.title: OBS-010
docs.text: Kind-specific edit controls: text kinds get one Text textarea; field gets Label + Field type select; field-group gets Label, an editable per-item field list, and Min/Max items; custom gets Label only; every panel ends with Cancel/Save; only one field may be expanded at a time. Explicit, High. (↩ used by BR-006, BR-007, BRULE-002)

docs.title: OBS-011
docs.text: Source (Known UX issues section): "unlinking opens a confirm dialog (names the sub-field cost for FieldGroups)... navigating away from a dirty edit ... prompts a discard-confirmation dialog." Explicit, High. (↩ used by BR-008, BR-014)

docs.title: OBS-012
docs.text: Source (Interactions & behavior section): "Add page/section/field, delete empty page/section, and reorder (page/section/field)... all are optimistic, no confirmation except unlink." Explicit, High. New line in v4 not present in the retracted v2 drop -- directly supports BRULE-007. (↩ used by BR-009, BRULE-007)

docs.title: OBS-013
docs.text: Search and confidence filters apply at the field level; a Section shows only if it has a matching field or its own heading matches; a Page shows only if it has a visible section; no pagination, no "expand/collapse all." Explicit, High. (↩ used by BR-004, BRULE-004)

docs.title: OBS-014
docs.text: "+ Add page" appends a new, empty, auto-numbered page (max existing + 1), renders expanded with just a "+ Add section" prompt, no confirmation dialog. Explicit, High. (↩ used by BR-009)

docs.title: OBS-015
docs.text: "+ Add section": inline form (title required, description optional), Add disabled until title is non-empty; saving creates a Section target plus a synthetic mapped heading (mappedBy: 'manual', confidence 100%). Explicit, High. (↩ used by BR-010)

docs.title: OBS-016
docs.text: "+ Add field": inline form (label required, field-type select), Add disabled until label filled; creates a Field target inserted immediately after that section, appears immediately with no reload. Explicit, High. (↩ used by BR-011)

docs.title: OBS-017
docs.text: Delete (trash) icon on a page/section appears only when it has zero children; deleting removes the target and any tied mapping; no confirmation dialog ("nothing to lose"). Explicit, High. (↩ used by BR-012, BRULE-003)

docs.text: What is the actual navigation trigger into the Mapping Report from elsewhere in the product? Originally raised as GAP-001 (the source itself never states this). docs.title: DEC-004
docs.text: Does reviewing or editing a workflow's mapping require a specific org role/permission, given the wider product shows org-level Members/Billing controls? docs.title: DEC-005
docs.text: What measurable signal would tell the team this feature is working (e.g. reduction in post-extraction correction time, or in downstream data-quality issues traced to a bad mapping)? The source states no success criteria for this feature at all -- not deferred, simply never addressed. Open, owner: Business Owner.

docs.title: GAP-001
docs.text: Unclear Behavior. Resolved 2026-09-08 via DEC-001 -- Human Provided evidence (OBS-021), not the design document.

docs.title: GAP-002

docs.title: GAP-003
docs.text: Conflict, Human Provided evidence vs. design source. The design source's own "Scope note" states manually-created workflows get no report at all ("don't build one"); OBS-021 instead describes the underlying structure editor as reused across all creation paths, including from-scratch. Resolved 2026-09-08 -- per PRODUCT-SOURCE-MATERIAL-SPEC.md section 6's authority rules, a direct Business Owner clarification on actual product behavior takes precedence over a design document's own scope text where they diverge. BR-015's original framing was too broad -- narrowed rather than removed; BR-016 added.

docs.title: GAP-004
docs.text:
Scope narrowing, Human Provided evidence vs. design source. The design source presents Card view (OBS-003, OBS-007) as a fully-built, first-class second rendering, on equal footing with Table view; OBS-025 (from the Review Outcome checklist) scopes the build to Table view only for this phase. Resolved 2026-09-08 -- same authority basis as GAP-003. Card view is not rejected -- it remains fully specified in the source for whenever it's prioritized -- only deferred out of the current build. BR-003's original framing (build both, kept in sync) was too broad for this phase -- narrowed, not removed; BRULE-005 kept as the modeling constraint for whenever Card view is picked up.

No contradiction-type gap remains open in this analysis. The retracted DA-002's internal-text contradictions were re-verified directly against v4 and found resolved -- see the correction note under the metadata table. GAP-003 and GAP-004 above are a different kind of finding -- real, newly-discovered tensions between the design document and direct Business Owner input, resolved by evidence authority, not leftovers from the prior analysis.

docs.title: TECH-001
docs.text: Business behavior known: each mapping arrives with a kind and a confidence score, already extracted from the PDF before the reviewer sees the report. Technical question: what extraction mechanism produces kind and confidence, and where does that processing happen? Related: CAP-001. For the Technical Agent stage -- not a business decision.

docs.title: TECH-002
docs.text: Business behavior known: reordering persists an explicit per-level override list, falling back to natural order for unmoved items. Technical question: what is the actual storage/sync mechanism for these override lists, and how do they interact with newly added or deleted items? Related: BR-013. For the Technical Agent stage -- not a business decision.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Find a mapping the extraction likely got wrong and fix it.

docs.text:
1. Select the "Low" confidence filter. (uses CAP-002)
